hints: Include a term for each power of the repeated factor $2x+3$.
Write $f(x)=\dfrac A{2x+1}+\dfrac B{2x+3}+\dfrac C{(2x+3)^2}$ and clear denominators.
Use $x=-\tfrac12$ and $x=-\tfrac32$ to find two constants, then compare a coefficient or use another $x$-value for the third.
walkthrough:
Set up the partial fraction decomposition for the rational function with repeated linear factor $(2x + 3)^2$:
$$\dfrac{10x + 9}{(2x + 1)(2x + 3)^2} = \dfrac{A}{2x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{2x + 3} + \dfrac{C}{(2x + 3)^2}$$

Multiply both sides by $(2x + 1)(2x + 3)^2$ to obtain the algebraic identity:
$$10x + 9 = A(2x + 3)^2 + B(2x + 1)(2x + 3) + C(2x + 1)$$

Substitute $x = -\dfrac{3}{2}$ to isolate $C$:
$$\text{LHS} = 10\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) + 9 = -15 + 9 = -6$$
$$\text{RHS} = A(0) + B(0) + C\left(2\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) + 1\right) = C(-3 + 1) = -2C$$
$$-2C = -6 \implies C = 3$$

Substitute $x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ to isolate $A$:
$$\text{LHS} = 10\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 9 = -5 + 9 = 4$$
$$\text{RHS} = A\left(2\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 3\right)^2 + B(0) + C(0) = A(-1 + 3)^2 = A(2)^2 = 4A$$
$$4A = 4 \implies A = 1$$

Equate the coefficients of $x^2$ to find $B$:
On the LHS, the coefficient of $x^2$ is $0$.
On the RHS, $A(2x + 3)^2 = A(4x^2 + 12x + 9)$ gives $4Ax^2$, and $B(2x + 1)(2x + 3) = B(4x^2 + 8x + 3)$ gives $4Bx^2$.
$$4A + 4B = 0$$
$$4(1) + 4B = 0 \implies 4B = -4 \implies B = -1$$

Verify by substituting $x = 0$:
$$\text{LHS} = 9$$
$$\text{RHS} = A(9) + B(3) + C(1) = 1(9) + (-1)(3) + 3(1) = 9 - 3 + 3 = 9 \quad \text{(verified)}$$

Write out the partial fractions expression:
$$\mathrm{f}(x) = \dfrac{1}{2x + 1} - \dfrac{1}{2x + 3} + \dfrac{3}{(2x + 3)^2}$$

ai_rubric.Partial Fractions: Identifies $\dfrac A{2x+1}+\dfrac B{2x+3}+\dfrac C{(2x+3)^2}$; Derives $A=1$, $B=-1$, $C=3$; Concludes with $f(x)=\dfrac1{2x+1}-\dfrac1{2x+3}+\dfrac3{(2x+3)^2}$.

hints: Integrate the three partial fractions from part (i) separately, including the factor $1/2$ from each linear denominator.
The squared-denominator term integrates to a reciprocal term, while the first two give logarithms.
Evaluate the antiderivative at $1$ and $0$, then combine logarithms with $\ln a-\ln b=\ln(a/b)$.
Keep an intermediate logarithm step visible before simplifying to the required exact form.
walkthrough:
Substitute the partial fractions into the definite integral:
$$\int_0^1 \mathrm{f}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int_0^1 \left(\dfrac{1}{2x + 1} - \dfrac{1}{2x + 3} + 3(2x + 3)^{-2}\right)\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate each term with respect to $x$:
- $\int \dfrac{1}{2x + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(2x + 1)$
- $\int \dfrac{1}{2x + 3}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(2x + 3)$
- $\int 3(2x + 3)^{-2}\,\mathrm{d}x = 3\cdot\dfrac{(2x + 3)^{-1}}{(-1)(2)} = -\dfrac{3}{2(2x + 3)}$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = 1$:
$$\text{At } x = 1: \quad \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{2(1) + 1}{2(1) + 3}\right) - \dfrac{3}{2(2(1) + 3)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right) - \dfrac{3}{2(5)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right) - \dfrac{3}{10}$$

Evaluate at the lower limit $x = 0$:
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{2(0) + 1}{2(0) + 3}\right) - \dfrac{3}{2(2(0) + 3)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) - \dfrac{3}{2(3)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$\text{Integral} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right) - \dfrac{3}{10}\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$$

Group the logarithmic and numerical components:
$$\text{Integral} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right) - \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right] + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{3}{10}\right)$$

Simplify the logarithm difference using $\ln A - \ln B = \ln(A/B)$:
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right) - \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \ln\left(\dfrac{3/5}{1/3}\right) = \ln\left(\dfrac{3}{5} \times 3\right) = \ln\left(\dfrac{9}{5}\right)$$

Combine to obtain the final exact result:
$$\int_0^1 \mathrm{f}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{9}{5}\right) + \dfrac{1}{5}$$

ai_rubric.Integrating Rational Functions: Integrates and derives $\frac12\ln(2x+1)-\frac12\ln(2x+3)-\frac3{2(2x+3)}$; Substitutes limits in an integral with terms $a\ln(2x+1)$, $b\ln(2x+3)$, and $c/(2x+3)$, where $abc\ne0$; Concludes with $\dfrac12\ln\dfrac59+\dfrac15$.
